name: Wipe transition
one_line: One scene replaced by the next through a moving edge or shape, not a cut or dissolve
summary: A moving edge or shape (a straight line, an expanding circle, a drawn silhouette) uncovers the next scene over the last. The change is visible and directional, so it can steer the eye, mark a new section or echo a graphic motif. A soft or flickering edge reads as accidental, and a wipe on every cut becomes a habit.

routes.one_line: Vector mask or clip shape swept across two layers on a seekable timeline

steps.does: Author the wipe shape as a vector clip or mask over the incoming scene
Move or scale the shape across the frame, seeked per frame

limits: Suits drawn vectors; masking supplied stills in SVG is untested
SVG evidence is one static raster by resvg; clip and mask rendering in a browser was not exercised
WAAPI evidence is transform, stroke draw and stagger; animating clip geometry is untested

routes.one_line: Two stills composited per frame through a mask that advances with t

steps.does: Build each frame's mask and composite incoming over outgoing still

limits: Suits supplied raster stills, and drawn vectors once rasterised; no live scenes
sharp evidence is one RGBA composite; mask-driven compositing and edge feather are untested
Per-frame image work is slow for long wipes; speed is outside the evidence scope

routes.one_line: Both scenes in one GPU scene, the top one revealed through an animated mask

steps.does: Reveal the incoming layer through a mask shape driven from t

limits: Suits supplied stills and drawn vectors; PixiJS evidence is Graphics geometry only
Masks, sprites and filters are outside the evidence scope
Mask edge antialiasing is not evidenced; check it at delivery size

source: references/fx §3; references/motion-director §4.3; tool records as of 2026-11-20
